statements.status_notes: GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf (CVE-2026-34180) is a heap buffer over-read in the OpenSSL copy bundled inside cryptography wheels when decoding crafted ASN.1 DER inputs larger than 2 GiB via d2i_X509(), d2i_PKCS7(), or related d2i_* entry points. The datahub-ingestion image uses cryptography only as a TLS client library for ingestion connectors (Snowflake, database sources, REST APIs) connecting to operator-configured endpoints; TLS handshake certificate chains and related ASN.1 objects are bounded well below 2 GiB, so an adversary cannot supply the pathological multi-gigabyte DER blob the flaw requires. A patched wheel requires cryptography>=48.0.1, but acryl-datahub 1.5.0.7 declares cryptography<47.0.0,>=46.0.5 on the snowflake and related extras in the slim install set, blocking an in-image bump until upstream lifts that cap.
